arguments.issue: The instruction asks for spec/typespec.toml's `[sample_stride]` entry to be typed `stride_int_kind` (for sampler arithmetic) AND typed `stride_text_kind` (so named presets still parse), while keeping a single `unit`. Looking at spec/load.py, a field has exactly one `kind` key (fields[section]['kind']), and spec/kinds.map defines stride_int_kind as backed by `integer` and stride_text_kind as backed by `string` — two mutually exclusive backings. A single TOML key can only hold one value, so `sample_stride` cannot simultaneously be both kinds under the current parser: whichever value is written last simply overwrites the other, silently breaking either arithmetic (if text wins) or preset parsing (if int wins), and there is no union/list support in load.py to hold both.
arguments.recommended_action: Either (a) confirm which single kind should actually win and accept the other capability is lost, or (b) authorize a real fix such as splitting into two fields (e.g. sample_stride_int / sample_stride_text) or extending load.py/kinds.map to support a list of kinds for one field, so both arithmetic and preset parsing can genuinely coexist. I don't want to write a spec that silently drops one of the two required behaviors while appearing to satisfy the request.
